title: Emergency: kernel cost-model miscalculation causing multi-environment TTFT spike
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Multiple customers reported sudden increases in time-to-first-token (TTFT) and dropped tokens/sec starting 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC. Incident spanned Hosted, several Dedicated pools, and one on-prem Private deployment. Root cause analysis points to a recent change to the kernel selection cost model (PR #7421) that misestimated memory-copy overheads for short-context, interleaved microbatches. The misestimate caused frequent selection of an end-to-end kernel path optimized for long sequences; combined with new prefetch/quarantine heuristics this produced microbatch thrash and extra memcpy/serialization, increasing TTFT and reducing tokens/sec for small-context chat workloads.

Observed impact: p50 TTFT increased from ~35ms to ~220ms for affected models on Hosted canaries; tokens/sec per-worker dropped by ~55% on Dedicated pools under mixed short/long context distributions. Private customer reported 3x higher cold-start time and sustained throughput loss. Several customer support tickets escalated (CS-1872, CS-1880).

Why this is urgent: regression surfaced on production traffic during peak hours; customer SLA-sensitive workloads (chat assistants, search re-ranking pipelines) were impacted, causing degraded UX and escalations to enterprise accounts. Immediate mitigation and a robust follow-up are required to prevent repeated regressions as we iterate the kernel cost model.
reproducer_steps: 1) Configure model redwood-7b-v2 with small context priming (prompt length < 80 tokens).
2) Send 1000 single-turn short messages at QPS 50 with varied interleaving of a few long requests (context > 1024 tokens).
3) Observe profiler traces: kernel selection path chooses long-sequence optimized kernels and triggers prefetch quarantine logic on >30% of requests.
4) Compare TTFT and tokens/sec to baseline runtime-2.3.0; significant delta expected in hosted canary and dedicated test pools.
telemetry_findings: Kernel selection telemetry shows ~42% of short-context requests routed to long-sequence kernel after PR #7421 (previously ~3%).
Memory copy time contribution to TTFT rose from median 5ms to 68ms on affected paths.
Prefetch quarantine helplink shows increased cache miss churn and extra serialization events correlating with TTFT spikes.
Dedicated pool workers saw 50-60% lower token throughput during the anomaly window; CPU scheduling and memcpy hotspots present in traces.
mitigation_plan: Immediate (hotfix): rollback kernel cost-model weights introduced in PR #7421 for production canaries and Dedicated pools (HOSTED rollback started 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC).
Emergency patch: force short-context heuristic to prefer legacy microbatch kernel path for models in affected_model list; disable prefetch quarantine for short contexts behind feature flag.
Canary rollout: deploy hotfix to 5% Hosted, monitor p50/p95 TTFT and tokens/sec for 15m before expanding to 50% and then 100% if stable.
Private remediation: provide a customer-facing patch bundle and deployment steps for on-prem kit; coordinate with Solutions (SE) for direct install.
rollout_notes: Canary began 2026-03-11 04:30 UTC on hosted-us-west-2 cluster id cluster-7
Rollback plan: if p95 TTFT does not improve by >=40% in 30 minutes, revert to runtime-2.3.0 tagged build and open rollback incident (INC-ROLLBACK-7674).
